plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds others' bids and pay only the second-highest bid, which never depends on your own bid. This maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' strategies. Since there's no history to suggest otherwise, and this is a one-shot game, I will bid exactly my value of $46 to ensure optimal expected payoff.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of others' bids. My value is $1, which is very low. Bidding above my value risks losing money if I win at a price above $1; bidding below risks losing a profitable opportunity. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. I'll bid exactly $1.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of other bidders' behavior. Since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. I'll bid my true value of $33.
